brief: A rapid rotation out of mega-cap tech and into small caps is underway, driven by falling bond yields: Russell 2000 outperformance over the Nasdaq has moved in lockstep with declining yields, a call BTIG's Krinsky is credited with making correctly. The move is historic in scale: the Nasdaq 100 just posted its worst monthly underperformance versus the equal-weighted S&P 500 since 2002, and Goldman's AI-at-Risk basket (GSPUARTI) had its second-worst month since ChatGPT launched. But the note flags signs the rotation is overextended. The Russell/NDX ratio's surge is one of the most aggressive in years even as its longer-term downtrend stays intact, Russell volatility has stayed contained despite the tech panic, NDX is testing major support at its 200-day moving average and trendline, and tech valuations have compressed to levels that are starting to look attractive. The conclusion stated is that reversal risk is rising, and chasing small-cap outperformance now may be just as dangerous as chasing tech was at its highs.
